findings.issue: contradicts task clause "or after the task's work is committed (when a phase review re-runs a task gate), copies exactly the base commit and reports 'lost: 0 lines'": sameness is judged over the WHOLE tree, so any non-ignored difference unrelated to the module or the suite makes the sides 'differ' and the comparison runs and exits 0 over a byte-identical module and suite - the same vacuous pass. Probe (scratchpad rd-probe/probe_same.py over a fixture checkout of the task tree's module): clean checkout `--base HEAD --head WORKTREE` -> exit 2 'the head is the base'; the same checkout plus one untracked `journal.jsonl` -> exit 0, 'lost: 0 lines reached at HEAD and not at WORKTREE', same False. The project checkout a phase review runs in is never that clean: the drive itself keeps docs/audit/journal/*.jsonl and docs/audit/evidence/* modified and writes untracked docs/audit/evidence/returns/<task>/ (git status of the project shows all three now), so the scenario the clause names still passes vacuously there. The docstring's 'Sides that differ anywhere, in any file, are measured: a task that changed nothing the suite reaches is an honest 0' states the hole as a property.
findings.resolution: Decide sameness on what the run can read, not on the whole tree: compute the differing paths (same_tree already walks both), print them, and treat the sides as the same (exit 2 unless --allow-same) when neither the module nor the suite differs and no differing path is a Python source (or, stricter, none lies under a directory on the suite's or module's import path). Add the other-direction case beside rd31: a clean fixture checkout plus one untracked non-.py file must still exit 2, and rd39 (a .py content change) must still be measured.

findings.issue: The recheck is accepted as evidence of chance whenever its blocks pass, its traces read, and per block its silent and untraced counts do not EXCEED the first run's. It never compares how many processes of a block wrote at all, nor how many cases ran. A rechecked block that passes having done less - a case that skips or bails early on its environment (a busy resource, a missing tool) and still grades ok, or a child that is never started - misses lost lines for a reason other than chance, and those lines are set apart under `sometimes:` with exit 0. Counts rather than identities also let an equal-count swap through (a different process of the block silent in the recheck than in the first run). So the claim 'it cannot set aside a real loss' holds only for a deterministic base; an environmental miss inside those bounds is set aside, not refused.
findings.resolution: Refuse with 2 also when a rechecked block wrote fewer processes than in its first run (count written dumps per block in read_traces, as silent_by_block already does for silent ones), or when its graded case count differs from the first run's; add a fixture case whose recheck skips the reaching case yet passes, expecting exit 2. And name the remaining blind spot (an equal-count swap of silent processes) under WHAT IT CANNOT SEE.

findings.issue: The bullet the brief names as this file's dependant is now inaccurate, not merely incomplete: it says the tool 'exits 1 naming each line of the module reached before and not after', but lines the recheck does not reach are now listed under `sometimes:` and exit 0; and its list of what 'refuses with 2 rather than passing' omits the two new refusals (the head is the base; a recheck that could not confirm a loss) and --allow-same. The executor answered this dependant as 'still correct but incomplete' and left it.

findings.issue: The diff changes the exit code of a command the plan's gates name. P152.4's and P152.17's gates are spelled `--base HEAD --head WORKTREE`; their work is committed, so a phase review re-running them now refuses with 2 on a clean tree (a red sign-off) and - per finding 1 - measures nothing and exits 0 on the drive's usual dirty tree. Neither reading measures the conversion those gates exist for.
findings.resolution: Re-point those gate entries to the commit before each task (`--base <pre-task sha> --head WORKTREE`, as P152.13's gate does with 92c399f5), which measures the conversion both before and after it is committed; use --allow-same only where identical sides really are the expected answer.

Add a selftest case: --base HEAD --head WORKTREE over a clean fixture checkout exits 2.'
